MoonPay vs Transak vs Banxa: Ramp APIs Compared
Compare documented ramp onboarding, KYC hand-offs, wallet controls and order tracking. Download a sourced MoonPay, Transak and Banxa dataset.
Reviewed by FluidRWA Research Team · October 23, 2026
Short answer

Start with how much of the customer journey you want to build. MoonPay documents APIs around its widget. Transak offers a Whitelabel API, but its current limitations exclude off-ramp and require a provider step for standard KYC. Banxa Native combines APIs and payment SDKs and requires account approval. These are different integration models, not a fastest-or-cheapest ranking.
Where does your customer go during checkout?

Decide how much of checkout your team will build. Then ask where customers complete identity checks and who helps when an order fails. Those answers will shape the integration more than the provider's API count.

What does this mean for your product team?

For a tokenized investment portal, walk through one investor's funding journey: select the asset and network, complete verification, make the fiat payment, receive the crypto and reconcile the order. Then repeat it with an unsuccessful payment and a customer who needs additional verification.

For a wallet app, start with the destination wallet and network controls. Ask which information the customer can change, what the provider validates and what support can recover after a mistake. An API accepting an address does not by itself establish those controls.

For a finance team, request a sample order record and a statement that can be matched to it. A webhook tells your application that something changed; it is not automatically a complete accounting record.
These are exercises for your pilot. FluidRWA has not run test transactions with these providers.
How should buyers evaluate onboarding?
Write down the customer country, payment method, fiat currency, asset, network and buy/sell direction.
Ask each provider to confirm that exact configuration, rather than comparing global coverage totals.
Draw the customer journey, including every verification screen and redirect.
Agree who answers the customer when verification or payment fails.
Demonstrate a delayed webhook and recover the order through an independent lookup.
Match the final order to fees, delivery evidence and any refund adjustment.

FAQ
Does this comparison establish which provider is best?
No. This is a public-documentation comparison of the existing cohort, not a ranked market sample or performance study. Verify the unresolved questions against your written buyer configuration.
Does a supported asset prove my customer can use it?

This dataset establishes no such assurance. Request confirmation for the exact geography, method, direction, amount, asset and network. Configuration discovery is not evidence of an approved production transaction.
Does Not verified mean a feature is absent?
No. The reviewed evidence did not establish the precise capability or responsibility. Ask for documentation, contractual confirmation or a controlled demonstration.
Is a white-label ramp also a white-label payment gateway?
Not necessarily. Fiat funding and merchant payment acceptance are different buyer tasks. Branding control alone does not establish custody, settlement or refund responsibilities.
Is successful KYC the same as permission to transact?
Do not treat them as interchangeable. Banxa's Native identity documentation distinguishes verification from transaction eligibility. Require a configuration-specific explanation of approval gates.
What is included in the CSV?

Eighteen observations across three providers and six buyer tasks, each with scope, an unresolved question, an exact primary-source URL and a row-level verification date. The full review is dated October 7; the Transak integration observation was updated October 23, 2026.
